title: How do you build a training matrix for a crypto business?
seoTitle: Training matrix for a crypto business
description: Build a crypto business training matrix: MiCA, VARA, FinCEN, AUSTRAC and AML duties by role and market, with frequency, evidence and an illustrative grid.
shortAnswer: A crypto business training matrix lists every role that touches customers, wallets, transactions or compliance against the training duties of each virtual asset regime the firm is licensed or registered under, such as MiCA and DORA in the EU, VARA in Dubai, FinCEN in the United States and AUSTRAC in Australia. Each cell then records a frequency, a trigger and the evidence that would satisfy that regime's supervisor.
keyTakeaways: Crypto firms are pulled into AML regimes as money transmitters, virtual asset service providers or crypto-asset service providers, so anti-money laundering columns dominate the matrix in every market.
Licensing regimes add role specific competence duties: MiCA Article 81(7) for staff who give advice or information, and VARA Rule I.J for every staff member of a Dubai licensee.

Only a few sources fix a clock. VARA requires operational policies to reach new hires within 30 calendar days and OFAC expects sanctions training at a minimum annually; most other intervals are the firm's own choice.
Agents, distributors, kiosk operators and outsourced compliance providers need rows of their own, because several regimes hold the principal responsible for their training.
MiCA's transitional period ended by July 1, 2026 at the latest, and the EU AMLR applies from July 10, 2027, so EU rows are moving now.

sections.heading: Why does a crypto business need its own training matrix?

blocks.text: Because a crypto firm is regulated through several doors at once: as a money transmitter in one country, a licensed virtual asset service provider in another, and an authorized crypto-asset service provider under EU law, each with its own training rule. A generic [compliance training](/glossary/compliance-training) catalog cannot show which of those regimes a given course satisfies.

The risks are also specific to the sector. The library's FinCEN page notes that training content for a virtual currency business should follow its risk assessment, such as blockchain analytics alerts, kiosk scam patterns, and mixing and anonymity enhancing techniques. OFAC's page places a virtual currency exchanger's sanctions risk in screening counterparties and wallet activity. Those risks belong in the rows, not buried in a general AML module.

The underlying method is the one in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix): roles on one axis, obligations on the other, and a rule in each cell. For a crypto firm the extra discipline is a market and license tag on every row, so the firm can produce a filtered view for each supervisor.

sections.heading: Which roles should a crypto firm list as rows?

blocks.text: List roles by the activity regulators attach duties to, not by team name. Virtual asset rules single out the governing body, the named compliance and money laundering reporting officers, people who advise or inform customers, and people who monitor transactions, so those become separate rows.

blocks.text: Treat these as [role based training](/glossary/role-based-training) groups: an engineer who moves into the monitoring team inherits the monitoring rows on the day of transfer.

sections.heading: Which training duties apply to crypto firms in each market?

blocks.text: The columns come from the regulation pages for each market where the firm is licensed or registered. Every summary below is drawn from a page that names crypto or virtual asset businesses in its scope.

items: **European Union.** MiCA Article 81(7) requires crypto-asset service providers that give advice to ensure the people giving advice or information on their behalf have the necessary knowledge and competence, and Article 68(5) requires all personnel to have the knowledge, skills and expertise their responsibilities need ([MiCA](/regulations/mica-staff-knowledge-and-competence)). DORA lists crypto-asset service providers among its financial entities, and Article 13(6) makes ICT security awareness and digital operational resilience training compulsory modules for all employees and senior management ([DORA](/regulations/dora-ict-security-awareness-training)). From July 10, 2027, AMLR Article 12 requires specific, ongoing, duly documented training, and its awareness requirement names Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on transfers of funds and crypto-assets ([EU AMLR](/regulations/eu-amlr-training-requirements)).

**United Arab Emirates.** In Dubai, VARA's Compliance and Risk Management Rulebook Rule I.J.4 requires training suitable for each role at the beginning of employment and on an ongoing basis, Rule I.J.5 requires AML/CFT training for all staff on a regular basis, and Part VI requires anti-bribery and corruption training for the board and all staff ([VARA](/regulations/vara-staff-training-requirements)). Federally, Cabinet Resolution No. 134 of 2025 Article 21(5) requires periodic programs and workshops for the compliance function and other relevant employees of virtual asset service providers ([UAE AML/CFT](/regulations/uae-aml-cft-training-requirements)).

**United States.** FinCEN treats convertible virtual currency exchangers and administrators as money transmitters, so 31 CFR 1022.210(d)(3) requires training of appropriate personnel, including detection of suspicious transactions ([FinCEN MSB AML](/regulations/fincen-msb-aml-program-training)). OFAC's Framework expects sanctions training for all appropriate employees at a minimum annually ([OFAC](/regulations/ofac-sanctions-compliance-training)).

**Australia.** Digital currency businesses are reporting entities, and section 5-9 of the AML/CTF Rules 2025 requires initial and ongoing training appropriate to each person's function, risks and responsibilities ([AUSTRAC AML/CTF](/regulations/austrac-aml-ctf-training-requirements)).

**Japan.** The Financial Services Agency (FSA) AML/CFT Guidelines apply to crypto asset exchange service providers, and section III-5 sets five required actions on hiring, training, content review, effectiveness and feedback ([FSA AML/CFT Guidelines](/regulations/japan-fsa-aml-cft-guidelines-training)).

sections.heading: What does a crypto training matrix look like when filled in?

blocks.text: It looks like a long list of role, market and obligation combinations, each with its own clock and evidence rule. The extract below is illustrative only, for a hypothetical exchange with a MiCA authorization in Portugal, a VARA license in Dubai, US money transmitter registration and an Australian registration. Where the frequency says firm policy, the firm chose it and must be able to justify it.

sections.heading: How should a crypto firm decide training frequency?

blocks.text: Start from the handful of fixed clocks, then set every other interval from the firm's risk assessment and record why. Most crypto rules say initial, ongoing, regular or periodic and stop there.

items: **Fixed clocks.** VARA Rule I.J.6: operational policies to new hires within their first 30 calendar days. OFAC Framework: at a minimum annually. Those two can be written into the matrix as stated.

**Examples, not minimums.** AUSTRAC gives 6 to 12 months for compliance officers and senior management and 12 months for customer facing staff as examples only, and says its own e-learning cannot be relied on solely.

**Change triggers.** VARA requires updated policies to be promptly communicated; the FSA FAQ expects training to be updated when the national risk assessment or FATF material changes and those already trained to be verified. New token listings, new chains or new typologies are natural internal triggers.

**Failure triggers.** OFAC expects immediate training or corrective action when testing or audit finds a deficiency. See [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) for ways to document the rationale.

sections.heading: What evidence will crypto supervisors expect to see?

blocks.text: Supervisors expect proof that each person understood the content relevant to their role, and records kept for the retention period each regime sets. Completion percentages alone will not answer the questions in the sources.

items: **Proving compliance.** VARA Rule I.F.1(c) requires a licensee to maintain sufficient records to prove compliance with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements, which includes training.
**Retention.** Cabinet Resolution No. 134 of 2025 Article 25 sets five year record retention in the UAE. OFAC's recordkeeping period in 31 CFR 501.601 rose to 10 years effective March 12, 2025.

**Testing that training works.** FinCEN's 2016 agent guidance names inadequate training as a material weakness that independent testing must detect, and the FSA has checked effectiveness verification through inspections since the 2025 program year.

**Assessment before the role.** AMLR Article 13 requires an assessment of skills, knowledge, expertise and integrity before people take up AML/CFT roles, repeated regularly, and AUSTRAC's section 5-8 sets a similar personnel due diligence duty. The guide on [evidencing training effectiveness to a regulator](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator) covers presentation.

sections.heading: Which crypto rule changes should already be in the matrix?

blocks.text: Several dates from the library's regulation pages, as at November 2026, change who is in scope or what the training must cover. Add them as dated rows so the status changes on the right day.

items: **July 1, 2026 at the latest, EU:** the MiCA Article 143(3) grandfathering period ended; Portugal notified 18 months. Firms still serving EU clients do so as authorized crypto-asset service providers.
**March 31, 2027, Australia:** first independent evaluation deadline for many existing reporting entities under the AUSTRAC transitional rules, which will test the training program.
**July 10, 2027, EU:** the AMLR applies directly, with Article 9 requiring a written training policy and Article 12 requiring documented, ongoing training.
**June 2028, Japan:** the FSA reports that Japan's FATF fifth round on-site assessment is scheduled, which raises the bar on evidence of effectiveness.

blocks.title: Still pending
blocks.text: ESMA's guidelines on criteria for assessing knowledge and competence under MiCA Article 81(7) were still marked final TBC in its July 2025 table, and FinCEN and OFAC proposed stablecoin issuer program rules under the GENIUS Act in April 2026. Track both as watch items, not matrix rows.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each crypto obligation to its market, license and source clause, and to the learning outcome and assessment point that satisfy it. When a rule such as MiCA or the AMLR moves, the affected roles and evidence rules are flagged for review. See [financial services](/industries/financial-services).

faqs.q: Does an offshore exchange with US customers need FinCEN training rows?
faqs.a: Likely yes. FinCEN guidance FIN-2019-G001 says the money transmitter rules, including the AML program and its training element, apply equally to foreign located convertible virtual currency money transmitters without a physical US presence when they do business wholly or in substantial part within the United States.

faqs.q: Do engineers at a crypto firm need AML training?
faqs.a: They need whatever their role requires. DORA makes ICT security awareness compulsory for all employees of a crypto-asset service provider, and MiCA Article 68(5) requires all personnel to hold the expertise their responsibilities need. Engineers who build monitoring rules or screening tools often also warrant AML content tied to those systems.

faqs.q: Can one AML course cover the EU, Dubai and the United States?
faqs.a: A shared core can, but each regime adds its own record. VARA requires AML/CFT training for all staff on a regular basis and new hire policy communication within 30 days, FinCEN requires suspicious transaction detection training, and the AMLR adds awareness of the transfer of funds and crypto-assets regulation. Map each module to the rule it meets.

faqs.q: Who signs off the crypto training plan?
faqs.a: Usually the named compliance roles, with board approval of the policy. VARA makes the Compliance Officer and MLRO responsible for staff training, the UAE Cabinet Resolution makes the compliance officer responsible for documented training plans, and AMLR Article 9 requires internal policies, including the training policy, to be approved by the management body.
